observations.content:
Summary: According to the sources, Sam Altman is currently serving as the CEO of OpenAI, a role he has held since 2019. However, there was a period in November 2023 when Altman was removed as CEO by the board, citing a lack of candor in his communications. Altman returned to the CEO position in December 2023, with Mira Murati returning as CTO and a new initial board consisting of Bret Taylor, Larry Summers, and Adam D’Angelo. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding Altman's current status beyond these events.

Early life [ edit ] Altman was born in Chicago on April 22, 1985, [ 5 ] to a Jewish American family. [ 10 ] At eight, Altman received his first computer—an Apple Macintosh —and began learning how to code and disassemble and examine computer hardware . [ 11 ] [ 12 ] He attended John Burroughs School , a private institution in Ladue, Missouri . [ 13 ] In 2005, after studying computer science for two years at Stanford University in Stanford, California , he dropped out without earning a bachelor's degree. [ 14 ] [ 15 ] Business career [ edit ] Early career [ edit ] In 2005, at the age of 19, [ 16 ] Altman co-founded Loopt , [ 17 ] a location-based social networking mobile application. [ 18 ] The company bought geolocation data from cellular providers and attempted to make an early social network for users to see where their friends were in real time. The board of Loopt attempted, twice, to remove Altman from his role as CEO, but Altman's supporters defended him and stated the attempts were not serious. [ 17 ] In March 2012, after Loopt failed to gain significant user traction, the company was acquired by the Green Dot Corporation for $43.4 million. [ 1 ] Y Combinator [ edit ] In 2011, Altman became a partner at startup accelerator Y Combinator (YC), initially working on a part-time basis. [ 19 ] In February 2014, he became president of YC, replacing YC co-founder Paul Graham , who had been his mentor. [ 17 ] Altman aimed to expand YC to fund 1,000 new companies per year and sought to broaden the types of companies funded, particularly focusing on "hard technology" startups. [ 20 ] In October 2015, Altman was involved in expanding YC's scope. He invested in multiple startups such as Stripe, Inc. . [ 17 ] In September 2016, Altman's role at YC expanded to president of YC Group, which included Y Combinator and other units.
